To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the IS industry is in a transition phase, (2) the knowledge/skill sets that recruiters look for in entry-level IS job applicants are changing, and (3) recruiters are not very satisfied with the current knowledge/skills that entry-level IS graduates are able to demonstrate.

the most important knowledge/skills for entry-level IS hires are: 1) the ability to communicate effectively, 2) the ability to think critically, 3) the ability to learn new technologies quickly, 4) the ability to solve business problems, and 5) the knowledge of the latest technologies.

the most important knowledge/skills that entry-level IS professionals should possess include: (1) the ability to communicate with non-IS professionals, (2) the ability to understand the needs of business users and translate them into IT requirements, (3) the ability to analyze and design information systems, and (4) the ability to use IT tools and technologies.
